purpose: Move managed release-pull-request policy from the GitHub composite-action shell script into a typed, provider-neutral Callisto decision boundary.
scope: The credential-free observation, deterministic decision, CLI JSON interface, GitHub snapshot collector, thin GitHub executor, and black-box contract tests for creating, updating, superseding, and retaining a Callisto-managed release PR.
non_goals: Making a GitHub pull request or its metadata release authority after merge.
Putting forge tokens, raw credentials, shell commands, or arbitrary GitHub API responses in durable release intent/state/receipt records.
Changing the merged-release-commit authority, artifact, or execute contracts from SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.

architecture.observation: The action gathers a small, credential-free snapshot of the configured repository's open managed PRs and branch workflow-delta facts. Callisto validates that snapshot against explicit configured base/release branch identity; it never accepts caller-side preselection of an existing PR.
architecture.decision: Callisto determines whether pending changesets require no PR, a new canonical PR, an update of exactly one canonical or SHA-suffixed managed PR, or a replacement PR. The decision names exact expected PR number/branch facts so the executor can detect a race before mutation.
architecture.execution: The composite action invokes `callisto release-pr decide`, then only executes the returned operation: version from the current base, stage the resulting worktree changes as a `callisto release-pr commit-plan` and materialize it on a deterministic staging branch via the forge's `createCommitOnBranch` commit API, verify the staged commit's tree is byte-identical to the local `git write-tree` result, move the real managed branch's ref onto that verified commit via a plain REST ref update, create or edit the named PR, and always delete the staging ref afterward. There is no local Git commit or `git push` anywhere in this path. It may render a body, manage a configured label, and re-observe expected state, but it does not independently choose an operation or branch.
architecture.authority: This is pre-merge collaboration policy, not durable release authority. After merge, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-FOUNDATION-007's parent-to-commit validation remains the sole release authority.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `callisto release-pr decide` accepts an explicit versioned snapshot and explicit configured base/release branch identity, computes whether the workspace has pending changesets, and emits a versioned JSON decision. It is read-only and does not invoke GitHub, push, write manifests, create a PR, tag, publish, or acquire ApplyPermit.

The decision model accepts only PRs from the configured repository whose head is either the exact canonical managed branch or its exact lower-case forty-hex SHA-suffixed replacement. Zero eligible PRs yields create; exactly one yields update; more than one fails closed. Lookalike prefixes, foreign repositories, malformed suffixes, a mismatched base branch, duplicate numbers, a PR whose head is the reserved deterministic staging branch itself, or unsupported schema versions fail before any mutation.

The commit materialized for an update or create decision always has the snapshot's base commit as its parent, and its change set never contains a `.github/workflows/*` path -- the commit-plan builder refuses such a path, any non-regular-file Git mode (executable bit, symlink, submodule), and any rename, copy, type-change, or unmerged path, all before the commit API is called. A managed branch that was already replaced under the prior SHA-suffixed-branch behavior (a `--<40-hex-sha>` suffix) remains a valid, ordinary managed branch and continues to be recognized and updated in place -- it is not migrated or renamed. A no-pending-changesets decision is a no-op and the executor performs no Git or GitHub mutation.

The GitHub action is a thin executor of the Callisto decision: it gathers the snapshot without caller-controlled jq filtering, calls the CLI, branches only on the closed decision kind, and rechecks the decision's expected PR/branch facts immediately before the ref move. Tests execute the exact script with recording Git/GitHub boundaries and demonstrate create, update, retained `--<sha>`-suffixed replacement branch update, no-op, stale-snapshot refusal before any mutation, a moved PR head caught before the ref move, a tree-mismatch refusal, staging-branch cleanup on failure, and that the script never invokes `git push`.

The CLI model and action outputs are credential-free, schema-versioned (schema version 2 for the snapshot/action/decision family), and stable for machine consumption. Diagnostics use typed miette errors on invalid snapshots; user-supplied PR body content is not persisted in the decision and remains body-rendering input only.

`ReleasePrCommitPlanV1::from_changes` always sets the plan's parent to the snapshot's base commit; it fails closed with a typed error on an empty change set, any `.github/workflows/*` or otherwise unsafe path (`.git/`, `..`, absolute, NUL), any non-regular-file Git mode, any rename/copy/type-change/unmerged path, and a payload over its documented conservative size cap. Each refusal has a dedicated passing test. Byte-fidelity between the plan and the actually-staged commit is proven by comparing the local `git write-tree` result against the staged commit's tree SHA, and this comparison is itself exercised by a passing test.

revision_note:
Extracted from SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013 after review identified that the existing Bash action was rediscovering create/update/supersede policy. This spec narrows the change to pre-merge release-PR collaboration while preserving the already specified post-merge durable authority boundary.

Amended after empirical testing against the real orin-dx/callisto public repository proved the prior supersede-branch mitigation was working around a symptom, not the cause. GitHub's built-in GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` through either the Git push protocol or the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` mutation's own `fileChanges`, on any ref -- confirmed by a real production failure (GitHub Actions run 33679599559, 2026-09-02: "refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow '.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml' without 'workflows' permission"). Supersede's SHA-suffixed replacement branches masked this by cutting a new branch whenever workflow files drifted, causing visible PR churn (#28 closed, #48 opened) with no underlying fix. Direct testing against the real repository confirmed the alternative: `createCommitOnBranch` restricted to only non-workflow paths succeeds (the commit inherits `.github/workflows/*` unchanged from its parent, so the mutation never touches that path), and a subsequent plain REST `updateRef(force)` moving a branch's ref onto that commit also succeeds even when the branch's prior `.github/workflows` content differed from the new commit's inherited content -- with the target branch's `.github/workflows` subtree ending up byte-identical to `main`'s. A ref move is not itself treated as writing `.github/workflows/*` by GitHub's restriction. `Supersede` is removed with no replacement; the commit-plan/staging-branch/ref-move sequence replaces it entirely.
